1254_2023.2_selection_event: The batch's scan quote ('Inwards RITC of liabilities - - -') is the 2023 roll-forward line, which is nil. The inwards RITC was in 2022: 'On 10th February 2022 and with effect from 1st January 2022, an inwards RITC was completed for Syndicate 2689, for 2017, 2018 & 2019 years of account. A premium of £75,243k ($101,578k) was received' (p38, p41); 2022 report p7: 'the Syndicate signed an inwards RITC for the 2019 and prior Years of Account for Syndicate 2689. The Syndicate received a premium of £75.2m'. It took effect at the opening of 2022, so before both diagonals of the 2023 table; no RITC, transfer or closure occurs in 2023 (the 2023 year of account is a new motor-injury quota share, p7). The syndicate is a legacy (run-off) vehicle: 'transaction of reinsurance business ... by way of reinsurance to close or other legacy solution'.
1254_2023.3_overlapping_history: Yes, restated history between the two reports for the taken-on years. The 2022 report's table (p30 image; same 2017-2019 columns, at 31 December 2022, 'estimates made by Syndicate 2689, i.e. prior to the RITC of the portfolio') prints: 2019: 38,332 / 68,611 / 71,562 / 57,689; 2018: 39,700 / 90,327 / 96,468 / 89,084 / 78,715; 2017: 35,747 / 62,114 / 62,914 / 65,996 / 64,390 / 60,403, with cumulative payments to date 36,692 / 53,916 / 50,922 and outstanding 20,997 / 24,799 / 9,480 (total 55,276, against 55,574 booked). The 2023 table's early cells are those scaled by 0.951 (sterling strengthened against the US dollar, the functional currency: 2019 36,426 against 38,332; 2018 37,782 against 39,700; 2017 33,985 against 35,747), but the end-2022 diagonal is not: 2019 66,295 against 57,689 (x0.951 = 54,862), 2018 82,754 against 78,715 (74,860), 2017 61,199 against 60,403 (57,440); in total 210,248 against 196,807 as printed (about 23.1m above on a like-for-like rate). Cumulative payments to date are also higher: 2023 table end-2023 payments 177,528 against 141,530 at end-2022 in the 2022 report, a rise of 36.0m, whereas the gross claims paid on those years in 2023 were about 20.8m (25,265 total less 4,493 on the 2023 year). No explanation of the restatement is printed in either report beyond the 'look through basis' sentence. In the 2022 report the diagonal at end-2022 is on the booked basis (it ties to 55,574) while the earlier cells are Syndicate 2689's: the 2022 table implies a 2022 incurred of -28.2m (57,689-71,562, 78,715-89,084, 60,403-64,390) against accounts 22,748 paid - 27,481 provision = -4.7m, because the take-on premium (£75.2m) was below 2689's own estimate.

1254_2023.6_reconstruct: Yes, to within 1.9m. The year t table's own two diagonals reproduce the year's gross incurred (2.3%) and the gross claims outstanding at both dates reconcile by a roll-forward (55,574 + 56,161 - 225 = 111,510; RITC line nil in 2023). The booked development of the taken-on years in 2023 is +8.7m, adverse (the report states 'Net prior year reserves on US casualty business were strengthened during 2023'), against M of +10.5m. The report restated the end-2022 diagonal and the cumulative payments between reports, so M cannot be taken from a comparison across reports, but within the 2023 table the two diagonals are consistent with the accounts.
1254_2023.reason: The concern is the earlier inward RITC of Syndicate 2689's 2017-2019 years (effective 1 January 2022) and a restated end-2022 diagonal in the 2023 table against the 2022 report (about 23m above on a like-for-like rate, with cumulative payments also restated). It is resolved at the level of M because the 2023 table's incurred ties to the accounts (2.3%), its closing provision ties exactly, and an independent bridge from the opening provision, 2023 payments and closing provision gives +8.7m for these cohorts against the table's +10.5m. The outcome is the development of the taken-on book (there are no other u <= 2021 cohorts), not an original-cohort figure.

1897_2019.2_selection_event: p33 note 15: 'The 2016 year of account Property class of business was transferred to the 2017 year of account under an RITC agreement. At the same time the cession between Syndicate 1897 and Syndicate 6126 on the 2016 year of account was increased from 85% to 100%. The 2016 year of account for Syndicate 6126 was reinsured to close (RITC) to Syndicate 3268. Syndicate 1897 (as the host syndicate) will still pay the claims on the Property class of business on behalf of Syndicate 6126 (now Syndicate 3268). The premium payable by Syndicate 1897 to Syndicate 3268 for the increase in the cession from 85% to 100% has not been settled', creditor 2,643. No date is printed in the note; a 2016 year of account closes at 36 months, 31 December 2018, so the closure falls at the opening of 2019 (year t), and the 2019 table's own end-2018 cells already show it (see 3). It touched the 2016 cohort (Property class) and, nominally, the 2017 year of account.
1897_2019.3_overlapping_history: Yes, one cohort restated, in both diagonals. Against the 2018 report (p37: 2016 column 55,393 / 102,295 / 105,882; all other columns scaled by 0.962-0.966, e.g. 2017 89,061 / 158,115 -> 85,818 / 152,163, 2011 22,769 -> 21,938, 2018 20,338 -> 19,594, the common factor of the consistent-exchange translation) the 2016 column in the 2019 table is 43,184 / 68,233 / 69,041 / 67,929: end-2018 69,041 against 105,882 x 0.963 = 102,000, i.e. about 33.0m (32%) removed at every age; the 2017 column was not increased (152,163 against 158,115 x 0.962 = 152,100). The net table shows the same removal on a smaller scale (2016 net end-2018 57,829 against 65,908 in 2018). So the 2016 Property class (about 33m of ultimate at end-2018, apparently about 9m of reserve: the 'FX and other' line of -15,356 exceeds the translation effect of about 6m) left the gross table and the gross balance sheet at 1 January 2019 and was not added to the 2017 row. Both diagonals used in M (2018 and 2019 cells) are on the restated basis, so the transfer does not enter M; the Property class's own 2019 development is outside it.
